text:
alex: Quick heads-up — I'm opening a small TF refactor PR to split our monolith module into network/compute/storage and unpin some providers. Wanted to call out the provider aliasing + secret path implications before anyone reviews.

maya: Thanks — can you paste the provider blocks? biggest concern is the registry->mirror swap we did last month and lockfile drift.

alex: Yeah. current provider block in module (before):
```hcl
provider "aws" {
  region = var.region
  version = ">= 3.0, < 4.0"
}
```
Planned change is to use aliased providers and the mirrored source: `registry.internal/acme/aws` and tighten constraints for stability. Also split modules will add `providers = { aws = aws.main }` to nested modules.

kevin: Two quick checks: 1) lockfile regen will show source changes for providers — CI plan step will fail until we update the lockfile. 2) state moves: tf may want to re-create resources if provider source or alias changes. We should plan a state mv strategy.

alex: Good call. My plan:
- create PR that only moves module code (no state change)
- run `terraform init -upgrade` locally with the mirror config and commit `terraform.lock.hcl`
- open a follow-up PR to change provider aliasing and run `terraform plan` in staging (no apply)
If plan looks sane, then do a targeted `state mv` for resources that changed provider meta.

sophie: For secrets: the compute module currently expects k8s secret at `namespaces/app/secrets/db-creds`. Splitting modules might move the k8s provider context. We need to keep the same secret path or update our k8s manifests to reference the new namespace. Did you update the module inputs?

alex: I added `k8s_namespace` input and defaulted it to the existing namespace so no immediate break. But the secret-wiring in our deployment repo will need a small change if ops wants a different namespace per environment.

maya: CI note — our plan pipeline gates on `terraform validate` + `terragrunt plan` (legacy) -> if the lockfile changes we currently have a lint step that rejects uncommitted lockfiles. So the PR will need the updated `terraform.lock.hcl` included.

kevin: Also, ensure provider source mapping is in `.terraformrc` for devs, or add a note in the PR template: `terraform providers mirror mapping required: registry.internal/acme/aws -> registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws` so people don't hit the 403 when fetching.

alex: Adding that to the PR description. One more gotcha: some resources reference `provider = aws.db` (aliased). When I split modules I used `providers = { aws = aws }` but that won't pass provider alias through unless we set `alias = "db"` in root. Might need to avoid aliases and instead pass in the same provider instance to nested modules.

sophie: If you can avoid alias proliferation that's great. For state mv, prefer `terraform state replace-provider` to reassign provider refs when source changes instead of moving each resource.

kevin: Yup — `terraform state replace-provider registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws registry.internal/acme/aws` is the least painful if the resource addresses/states are identical.

alex: Good tip — I'll test `state replace-provider` in a clone of staging state first.

infra-bot: deploybot: plan pipeline for PR #4123 started by alex — status: queued

maya: Also, small request — could you add a smoke plan artifact screenshot in the PR so reviewers can see there are no drifting deletes? quick `/workspace/plan.out` screenshot is fine.

alex: Will do. Tagging @kevin and @sophie for final signoff before I merge the lockfile PR.

kevin: quick look now — code side lgtm, but please attach lockfile and the `terraform version` you ran locally.

sophie: lgtm from infra side, just keep the secret namespace default as-is and we can handle any environment overrides later. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks everyone — PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123 — I'll push lockfile in a minute and update the PR description with the `.terraformrc` mapping and `state replace-provider` steps I ran.

maya: awesome — ping here when the lockfile is pushed, we'll kick the CI. :rocket:
